P1.text: Core change, one node: createContext takes only a key and Context has only key. $getContext throws a named error that carries the context key when no provider above set it, on the server and in the browser. Delete the defaultValue fallbacks (server.ts:805, client/context.ts:62,129,237), the CONTEXT_ADDED hook and the madeContexts and waitingReads maps. routeContext and navigationContext lose their defaults because the runtime already provides both to every page.

P2.text: Optional reads get one explicit, local primitive: a compile-time $hasContext(Context) that returns whether a provider above set it. Contexts are static since #469, so the answer is fixed when the scope is made and keeps the graph static. A part that works with no provider writes `$hasContext(C) ? $getContext(C) : fallback`, and the fallback is built per reader, so it is never module-global and cannot cross requests (J5). It mirrors the `has` of Svelte 5's createContext triplet.

evidence.detail: Svelte 5.40 createContext() returns [get, set, has]; get throws if set was not called in an ancestor; has is the optional read

O1.text: P2 does not fit $store. Readers bind a store at the top level with `const x = $store(given.state)` or `$store(LabelContext)`, and $store accepts only a context or one key of a $getContext value (BRM194 otherwise). `$hasContext(C) ? $getContext(C) : fallback` gives no store to bind, so the 50 store(null) readers cannot be migrated until $store gains an optional or conditional form. That is a third compiler change that P2 and P3 do not cost.

P9.text: $hasContext is a compile-time `$` function exported from brumate/signals beside $getContext, and is added to the list at decisions.md:7. Call: `$hasContext(Context)` returns a boolean. Server: it runs the same walk up the scope parents that $getContext uses, and returns true when a node above holds the key or the key is ROUTE_KEY. Browser: it calls findProvider on the page state (J11), so no new resume data and no new flag. Providers are static (#469), so the answer is fixed when the scope is made and never changes while the page lives.

P10.text: Answer to O1, exact optional form: a second argument, the literal `true`, on $getContext and on $store. `$getContext(C, true)` returns undefined when no provider is above. `$store(source, true)` takes the same sources as today (a context, or a key of a $getContext value, BRM194 otherwise) and gives undefined when the provider is missing. Ui readers write `const g = $getContext(C, true); const x = $store(g?.state, true)` or `const x = $store(C, true)`; the compiler accepts `g?.state` only when g came from `$getContext(C, true)`. The variable x is undefined without a provider, and the optional form allows only const, so a new BRM error covers `let` and no write reaches a missing store. Server: the read finds no value and records no store link in the page state. Browser: findStore finds no provider on resume (J11), so linkRead and waitingReads are not used and x stays undefined. The compiler checks the literal, so the graph stays static.

evidence.source: J10, J11, error-catalog.ts BRM194 and client/context.ts findStore/linkRead on feat/context-stores
evidence.detail: this adds one optional argument to $getContext and to $store, not a new function; ui readers that today test `state` for null test the variable for undefined instead

O8.text: P10 gives two optional-read forms, `$hasContext(C)` and the `true` flag, but the user chose $hasContext alone (Q1, Svelte's get/set/has). Svelte has no optional get, so the flag goes past the answer. It also adds a second meaning to the return of $getContext and $store (value or undefined), a rule that `g?.state` is accepted only when g came from a flagged read, and a new BRM code for `let`. That is more compiler surface than the guard it replaces.

O9.text: Use $hasContext alone and narrow $store to a guarded form: the compiler accepts `const x = $hasContext(C) ? $store(C) : undefined` (and the same with `$store(g.state)` where g is `$hasContext(C) ? $getContext(C) : undefined`) as one recognised shape. The guard is the user's own primitive, the branch is a compile-time fact (P9, static providers), and no flag, no second return type and no `?.` rule are added. N2 shrinks to $hasContext plus one pattern check in the $store analysis, and readers keep one idiom.
